record.original_question: Investigate how zero-density estimates depend on available moment bounds for the Riemann zeta function. In particular, Ingham’s method uses the fourth moment integral over [T, 2T] of |zeta(1/2 + it)|^4 dt; determine whether other nontrivial moments, such as Heath-Brown’s twelfth-moment estimate, can be used in zero-density arguments, and whether analogous arguments can be generalized to other L-functions.

evidence.quote: Investigate the dependence of zero-density on moments of the zeta-function? More specifically, Ingham’s zero-density estimate makes use of the fourth moment ... Can we use other non-trivial moments (like, say, Heath-Brown’s estimate of the 12th moment) in such zero-density results, and can we generalise this to other L-functions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\zeta(s)$ denote the Riemann zeta function, and for $\sigma \in [1/2, 1]$ and $T \geq 2$ let
$$N(\sigma, T) = \#\{\rho = \beta + i\gamma : \zeta(\rho) = 0,\ \beta \geq \sigma,\ 0 < \gamma \leq T\}.$$
A zero-density estimate is a bound of the form $N(\sigma, T) \ll T^{A(\sigma)(1-\sigma)} (\log T)^{B}$ for some functions $A(\sigma)$ and $B$. Ingham's classical zero-density estimate is derived using the fourth-moment bound
$$\int_T^{2T} |\zeta(\tfrac{1}{2}+it)|^4 \, dt \ll T (\log T)^4,$$
together with mean-value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials. Heath-Brown established the twelfth-moment bound
$$\int_0^{T} |\zeta(\tfrac{1}{2}+it)|^{12} \, dt \ll T^{2}(\log T)^{17}.$$

(a) Develop a general framework that converts a nontrivial $2k$-th moment estimate for $\zeta(\tfrac{1}{2}+it)$ (for $k > 2$, e.g., Heath-Brown's twelfth-moment bound) into a zero-density estimate for $N(\sigma, T)$, and determine precisely the dependence of $A(\sigma)$ on the moment exponent $k$ and on the strength of the available moment bound.

(b) Determine whether such moment-based zero-density arguments can be extended to general $L$-functions $L(s, \pi)$ associated to automorphic representations $\pi$ (in particular Dirichlet $L$-functions and $L$-functions in the Selberg class), and identify the analytic inputs (mean values, approximate functional equations, large-sieve-type inequalities) required for the generalization.
artifact.category_tag: Zero-density estimates and moments of L-functions
artifact.status_search_result: The interplay between moment bounds and zero-density estimates is a classical and ongoing area. Heath-Brown's 1979 work already derived zero-density estimates for $\zeta$ and Dirichlet $L$-functions using sixth- and higher-moment-type inputs, and recent work (e.g., Guth–Maynard 2024 on large values of Dirichlet polynomials, and surveys on density theorems) continues to refine $A(\sigma)$. While substantial partial results are known, a complete description of the optimal trade-off between moment strength (including Heath-Brown's twelfth moment) and zero-density exponents, and full generalization to all $L$-functions, remains open.

status_evidence.title: Zero Density Estimates for the Riemann Zeta-Function and Dirichlet L-Functions (Heath-Brown, 1979)
status_evidence.snippet: Heath-Brown derived zero-density estimates using higher moment inputs for both the Riemann zeta function and Dirichlet L-functions.
status_evidence.claim: Moment-based zero-density methods have been partially developed for Dirichlet L-functions.

status_evidence.title: Moments and zero density estimates for Dirichlet L-functions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies how hypotheses on higher moments of Dirichlet L-functions can extend the range of validity of zero-density estimates.
status_evidence.claim: The dependence of zero-density on higher moments has been studied for Dirichlet L-functions but is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Large values of Dirichlet polynomials and zero density estimates for the Riemann zeta function (Guth–Maynard)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent improvements on zero-density estimates via large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of optimizing zero-density estimates via analytic inputs remains an active research area.
